col5_Comment: CONTINUITY OF ELECTRICITY SUPPLY\nThe continuity of electricity supply is assessed using a nationally defined indicator shared with the CRE (French Energy Regulatory Commission), which the concessionaire monitors over time: the B criterion. It measures the time, expressed in minutes, during which a customer supplied at Low Voltage is, on average, deprived of electricity, regardless of the cause of the supply interruption (maintenance work or fortuitous incident on the public distribution network, incident upstream of the public electricity distribution network). With 26.3 minutes in Paris in 2022, the all-cause B criterion (TCC) shows an increase of 7.6 minutes compared to the previous year (18.7 minutes of B criterion TCC in 2021), particularly affecting the part excluding exceptional events related to Distribution (HIX excluding RTE), which records a significant increase: 24.9 minutes compared to 17.2 minutes in 2021 (+7.8 min).The \'incident\' portion has seen a significant increase compared to the previous year (20.8 minutes compared to 11.2 minutes in 2021) in a context of climatic hazards that marked the year 2022: intense and prolonged summer heatwaves in June (from June 17 to 27), July (from July 15 to August 1), and August (from August 13 to 18). These heatwave episodes generated a cumulative HTA incidents B criterion of 7.9 minutes and a BT incidents B criterion of 1.4 minutes, accounting for nearly half of the incidents B criterion in 2022.\nAll these informations have been provided by Enedis [confidential - Paris' decisional report each year]

question_text: Report the following information on access to secure energy for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Percentage of population or households with access to electricity
col2_Indicator^: Percentage of households with access to electricity (%)
col5_Comment: Electricity access in Ankara is universal. According to the Turkish Statistical Institute (TUIK) and the Energy Market Regulatory Authority (EMRA), 100% of households are connected to the national grid. No community depends exclusively on off-grid supply, although rooftop photovoltaic installations exist in some districts. The Ankara Metropolitan Municipality (AMM) confirms in its Greenhouse Gas Inventory (YIDEP, 2019) that household and non-residential consumption is fully grid-based. For this assessment, household bills were used to verify access and confirm actual usage. Minor outages occur but are short and localized, not affecting secure access overall. Vulnerable groups are not excluded from the grid, and universal electrification has been stable for decades. This indicator aligns with the Global Covenant of Mayors (GCoM) Energy Access and Poverty Pillar.

question_text: Report the following information on access to secure energy for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Average duration of available electricity
col2_Indicator^: Number of hours electricity is available per day (hours/day)
col5_Comment: Ankara benefits from a reliable grid operated by the Turkish Electricity Transmission Corporation (TEIAS) under EMRA oversight. Electricity is available on average 24 hours/day. TEIAS reports show annual outage duration below 1% of supply time, comparable with OECD cities. Household bills and AMM's Greenhouse Gas Inventory (YIDEP, 2019) confirm continuous service to households and businesses. Outages due to maintenance or weather are rare, temporary, and localized. Therefore, the value is reported as 24 hours/day. Household billing records also validate that service continuity is effectively universal, as all households report monthly consumption without interruption. The AMM coordinates with TEIAS and EMRA to maintain high reliability and improve response times.

question_text: Report the following information on access to secure energy for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Average yearly final energy consumption per capita
col2_Indicator^: kWh/year/person
col5_Comment: Final electricity consumption per capita in Ankara is estimated at ~2,800 kWh/year/person in 2019. The value was calculated from total electricity consumption in the AMM Greenhouse Gas Inventory (YIDEP, 2019), divided by the city population. Household bills and aggregated utility data were used to confirm this value. The indicator includes both residential and non-residential electricity use, consistent with national averages. Other energy sources (natural gas, LPG, coal, district heating) are excluded. Monitoring per capita consumption provides insight into socio-economic development and dependency on secure grid infrastructure. Household billing data is crucial, offering a transparent method to validate consumption levels and seasonal variations. Continuous monitoring allows AMM to plan for demand management and renewable integration, aligning with GCoM's “Secure Energy” framework.

col5_Comment:
Data Akses Listrik Rumah Tangga :
Jumlah pelanggan listrik rumah tangga Kota Medan tahun 2023 = 469.244 pelanggan
Jumlah rumah tangga Kota Medan (BPS 2023) = ± 472.000 rumah tangga.
Sekitar 99,4% rumah tangga di Kota Medan telah memiliki akses listrik pada tahun 2023.

Kota Medan hampir mencapai elektrifikasi penuh dengan tingkat akses 99,4%.

Tantangan ke depan lebih fokus pada:
1. Kualitas layanan listrik : meminimalkan pemadaman dan memperpanjang durasi pasokan.
2. Transisi energi bersih : meningkatkan porsi listrik dari energi terbarukan.
3. Menyediakan tarif terjangkau untuk rumah tangga miskin agar tidak hanya memiliki akses tetapi juga dapat memanfaatkan listrik secara optimal.

question_text: Report the following information on access to secure energy for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Average duration of available electricity
col2_Indicator^: Number of days electricity is available per year (days/year)
col5_Comment:
Durasi rata-rata listrik tersedia menunjukkan berapa jam per tahun listrik menyala tanpa gangguan.
1. Dalam kondisi ideal: 8.760 jam/tahun (24 jam × 365 hari).
2. PLN mengukur ini menggunakan SAIDI (System Average Interruption Duration Index) dan SAIFI (System Average Interruption Frequency Index).

Berdasarkan Statistik PLN 2023:
1. SAIDI Sumatera Utara = 6,98 jam/tahun
(rata-rata lama pemadaman per pelanggan dalam setahun).
2. SAIFI Sumatera Utara = 4,72 kali/tahun
(rata-rata frekuensi pemadaman per pelanggan dalam setahun)
Kota Medan sebagai ibu kota provinsi umumnya memiliki kinerja lebih baik dari rata-rata provinsi, sehingga SAIDI diperkirakan 5-6 jam/tahun.

Perhitungan Durasi Listrik Tersedia :
Jika SAIDI = 6,0 jam/tahun 

Durasi tersedia=8.760−SAIDI
 8.760 - 6,0 = 8.754 jam/tahun 

Persentase ketersediaan= (8.754 : 8.760) × 100 
 = 99,93%

Rata-rata pelanggan di Kota Medan mengalami pemadaman listrik ±5-6 jam sepanjang tahun 2023.
Listrik tersedia selama 99,93% waktu dalam setahun, setara dengan 24 jam penuh hampir setiap hari.

Komponen	 Nilai

Jumlah penduduk Kota Medan : 2.474.166 jiwa
(2023, BPS)	
Estimasi total energi final : 10.750.000 MWh
(termasuk BBM & LPG)	

Perhitungan Konsumsi Energi Final Per Kapita yaitu:

Energi per kapita = (Total konsumsi energi : 
 Jumlah penduduk) 
 = (10.750.000 MWh : 
 2.510.000 jiwa) 
 = 4,34 MWh/kapita/tahun
Rata-rata setiap penduduk Kota Medan menggunakan 4,34 MWh energi per tahun, termasuk listrik, BBM, dan LPG.

question_text: Report the following information on access to secure energy for your jurisdiction.
row_name: Average yearly final energy consumption per capita
col5_Comment:
Según el Diagnóstico Energético Local de Montería (2016):
•El consumo total de energía final fue de 1 399 GWh/año (equivalente a 1 399 000 MWh), distribuido así:
oElectricidad: 45 %
oCombustibles (transporte, térmico, GLP): 55 %
Ciudad Energética
•La población estimada en ese momento era de aproximadamente 513 000 habitantes (dentro de lo que hoy se considera la zona municipal y su área metropolitana) Wikipedia.
Con estos datos, el consumo final per cápita se puede calcular como:
Consumo per cápita= (1399GWh / 513000 personas) ≈ 2,728 kWh/persona/año 
En otras palabras: 2 728 kWh por persona al año, incluyendo energía usada en electricidad y combustibles para cocina, transporte, calefacción, etc.
Consumo total de energía final: 1 399 GWh/año
Población referida ~513 000 habitantes
Consideraciones importantes
•Este valor corresponde al año 2016, que es el más reciente con inventario local disponible.
•No dispone de desglose posterior (por ejemplo, 2022 o 2023) específico para Montería, aunque el patrón nacional muestra progresivo aumento de consumo per cápita conforme crece ingreso y acceso DANE+1.
•Para indicadores más actualizados sería necesario acceder a informes más recientes del municipio, DANE o expedientes del Ministerio de Minas y Energía.
conclusión
En Montería, el consumo anual promedio de energía final por persona (suma de electricidad y combustibles para todos los usos) era de aproximadamente 2 728 kWh en 2016.

col5_Comment:
Electricity in Taiwan is centrally coordinated and supplied by the state-owned Taiwan Power Company (Taipower), ensuring universal access to energy for all citizens. According to Taipower's 2023 Sustainability Report, Taiwan's residential and industrial electricity prices ranked as the fifth-lowest and third-lowest in the world, respectively. The average electricity price was approximately NT$3.12 per kilowatt-hour.

Except where restricted by laws or regulations, Taipower provides electricity services upon request, achieving a 100% application fulfillment rate.

For the small number of households without access to electricity, the main reasons are: (1) residing in remote areas where power infrastructure is unavailable; and (2) electricity disconnection due to unpaid bills arising from financial hardship. These households have been classified as low-income and are eligible for financial or material assistance provided jointly by the government and charitable organizations.

col5_Comment:
Berdasarkan publikasi Kota Pontianak Dalam Angka 2025 (BPS Pontianak), total energi listrik yang terjual kepada pelanggan PLN di wilayah Pontianak sepanjang tahun 2024 tercatat sekitar 1,263.242.086 kWh (sekitar 1,263 TWh). Angka ini mencakup konsumsi listrik dari semua golongan pelanggan (rumah tangga, bisnis, industri, sosial, kantor pemerintah, dll.) yang dilayani PLN di Pontianak pada tahun tersebut. Perlu dicatat: Data PLN Pontianak disajikan per Unit Layanan Pelanggan (ULP) dan mencakup beberapa area di sekitar Kota Pontianak (seperti wilayah tertentu di Kabupaten Kubu Raya). Namun, dalam statistik resmi BPS, angka tersebut dianggap mewakili konsumsi listrik Kota Pontianak secara keseluruhan.

Jumlah Penduduk Kota Pontianak (2024)

Untuk menghitung konsumsi per kapita, diperlukan data jumlah penduduk. BPS mencatat estimasi jumlah penduduk Kota Pontianak pada pertengahan tahun 2024 sekitar 680.852 jiwa. Angka ini merupakan hasil proyeksi penduduk tahun 2020-2035 (berdasarkan Sensus Penduduk 2020) dan digunakan sebagai perkiraan populasi Kota Pontianak tahun 2024.

Perhitungan Konsumsi Listrik per Kapita 2024

Dengan total konsumsi listrik ~1,263 miliar kWh dan populasi ~680,852 jiwa, dapat dihitung konsumsi listrik rata-rata per kapita sebagai berikut:

Konsumsi per kapita = (Total konsumsi listrik tahunan) / (Jumlah penduduk)

Konsumsi per kapita 2024 = 1.263.242.086 kWh / 680.852 jiwa ≈ 1.855 kWh per kapita per tahun.

col5_Comment:
Porcentagem de residências com acesso à eletricidade (100%) - Ano-base 2022

O valor de 100% de residências com acesso à eletricidade foi obtido a partir do Censo Demográfico 2022, conduzido pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), especificamente na tabela 8127 do sistema SIDRA, que apresenta a distribuição dos domicílios particulares permanentes por tipo de combustível para cozinhar e por acesso à rede elétrica. Os resultados confirmam que praticamente todos os domicílios de Vitória de Santo Antão (PE) possuem ligação à rede pública de energia, tanto em áreas urbanas quanto rurais, indicando cobertura universal do serviço.

A escolha desse indicador - porcentagem de residências com acesso à eletricidade - segue o padrão internacional utilizado pelo CDP-ICLEI Track e pelos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS 7), garantindo comparabilidade com outros municípios. A disponibilidade do dado foi classificada como “disponível para reportar”, pois se baseia em levantamento censitário atualizado e publicamente acessível, de alta confiabilidade metodológica.

Essa métrica expressa a dimensão de acesso físico à energia, sendo fundamental para avaliar a inclusão energética e a universalização dos serviços básicos. Ao alcançar 100%, Vitória de Santo Antão demonstra que a infraestrutura elétrica cobre integralmente o território, embora persistam desafios de pobreza energética em termos de capacidade de pagamento e uso adequado da energia, tratados em outros indicadores do CDP.
📊 Fonte: https://sidra.ibge.gov.br/tabela/8127

row_name: Average duration of available electricity
col2_Indicator^: Number of hours electricity is available per year (hours/year)
col5_Comment:
Duração média da eletricidade disponível (8.750 horas/ano) - Ano-base 2023

O valor de 8.750 horas/ano representa a estimativa de disponibilidade média anual da eletricidade no município de Vitória de Santo Antão, considerando os indicadores oficiais de continuidade do fornecimento divulgados pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL). O dado tem como base o DEC (Duração Equivalente de Interrupção por Unidade Consumidora) e o FEC (Frequência Equivalente de Interrupção) da distribuidora Neoenergia Pernambuco, responsável pelo atendimento local.

Em 2023, o DEC médio anual da concessionária foi de aproximadamente 9 a 10 horas, o que significa que o fornecimento de energia esteve disponível mais de 99,9% do tempo. O cálculo da disponibilidade resulta de subtrair o valor do DEC das 8.760 horas existentes em um ano, resultando em aproximadamente 8.750 horas de energia disponível.

A escolha do indicador “número de horas de eletricidade disponível por ano” está em conformidade com o protocolo do CDP, pois traduz diretamente a confiabilidade do serviço elétrico e a resiliência da infraestrutura energética. A informação é considerada disponível para reportar, uma vez que é atualizada anualmente, auditada pela ANEEL e amplamente reconhecida como referência oficial de qualidade de fornecimento no Brasil.
⚡ Fonte: https://www.aneel.gov.br/ranking-de-desempenho-das-distribuidoras

row_name: Average yearly final energy consumption per capita
col2_Indicator^: kWh/year/person
col5_Comment:
Consumo médio final anual de energia per capita (1.530 kWh/pessoa/ano) - Ano-base 2023

O consumo médio final anual de 1.530 kWh/pessoa/ano foi calculado a partir do consumo total municipal de eletricidade e da população estimada. O valor total de consumo (≈ 220.000 MWh/ano) foi obtido a partir das séries da ANEEL e da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE), enquanto a população de referência (≈ 144.000 habitantes) foi extraída das Estimativas Populacionais do IBGE para 2025.

A escolha do indicador “kilowatt-hora por pessoa por ano” reflete a métrica internacionalmente adotada para comparar níveis de consumo energético per capita entre cidades. Essa abordagem facilita a avaliação da eficiência energética, do nível de desenvolvimento econômico e do padrão de vida da população. O dado foi considerado disponível para reportar, pois combina estatísticas oficiais de fácil acesso e metodologia transparente, baseada em cálculos diretos e verificáveis.

O ano-base 2023 foi escolhido por ser o mais recente com dados consolidados de consumo municipal de eletricidade e alinhado ao Balanço Energético Nacional (BEN 2024). O valor obtido está coerente com a média de municípios de porte médio de Pernambuco, confirmando a adequação metodológica da estimativa.
🔋 Fontes:
	•	https://www.epe.gov.br/pt/publicacoes-dados-abertos/publicacoes/balanco-energetico-nacional-2024
	•	https://sidra.ibge.gov.br
	•	https://www.aneel.gov.br
